notes:
Intro/summary:
- Enterprise evaluation focused on Dedicated capacity sizing for customer-facing chat + reranking flows (low-latency fraud signals integration).
- Customer wants SLA/throughput guarantees for peak trading windows; careful on data residency and retention.

Workshop recap (2/18 on-site):
- Attendees: AE (Priya), SE (Liam), Nimbus engineering (Head of Infra + ML Eng), Security (Head InfoSec), Procurement.
- Covered: baseline workload profiling, peak vs steady-state modelling, reserved GPU economics, proposed SLAs and escalation paths.
- Fireflies id: ff-3f4e2-2026-02-18 (transcript uploaded).

Baseline workload (customer-provided telemetry):
- Primary flow: real-time chat assistant for account managers + automated reranking of transaction alerts.
- Observed steady-state QPS: ~15 req/s (business hours), avg prompt tokens 50, avg completion tokens 150 -> ~200 tokens/req.
- Steady-state token rate: 15 * 200 = 3,000 tokens/s.
- Peak windows: scheduled market events -> short bursts up to 5x steady-state (peak ~75 req/s -> 15,000 tokens/s).
- SLA target: 99.9% availability for API, p95 latency target for end-to-end response < 800ms for typical 200-token outputs.

Dedicated sizing recommendations (workshop output):
- Model variants to test in 48-hr POC: 1) Llama-3-70B-quant (fp16+4-bit q), 2) Llama-3-13B-optimized, 3) customer-finetuned 13B variant.
- Measured median token throughput (estimates for planning): H100 perf ~6,000 tok/s per GPU (sustained, with batch/windowing); A100 perf ~3,500 tok/s per GPU.
- Steady-state plan: reserve 2 x H100 (N+1 redundancy) to cover 3,000 tok/s comfortably and allow rolling upgrades.
- Peak plan / burst capacity: autoscale to 4 x H100 for short windows (handles ~24,000 tok/s headroom). Use burst credits for monthly peaks to avoid long-term commit.
- If using A100 (customer preference in one cluster): reserve 4 x A100 steady-state, autoscale to 8 x A100 for peaks.
- KV cache recommendation: enable prefix caching for sessioned users to cut token generation by ~20-35% (saves compute during steady-state).

SLA & commercial negotiation notes:
- Customer requests 99.95% for dedicated pool; Redwood proposed 99.9% with 30-minly incident updates and SRE escalation path.
- Penalty structure: credits-based; Nimbus pushed for defined uptime credit tiers and a separate SLA for peak-capacity guarantees (we proposed SLA for steady-state, best-effort for market spike bursts).
- Data residency and audit: require KMS integration + audit_logging for all token inputs; retention controls for 365 days default, ability to purge on demand.

Security & compliance actions (open):
- Provide SOC2 Type II evidence + ISO27001 scope mapping (owner: Security, due 3/16).
- Run security POC: air-gapped secret injection test in their VPC (SE: Liam).
- Provide encryption-in-transit and at-rest whitepaper + KMS integration steps.

Next steps / Milestones:
- 3/11: Confirm model binaries and dataset slices for 48-hr throughput workshop. (owner: Liam)
- 3/16-3/18: Run 48-hr dedicated throughput workshop in Nimbus VPC (on-prem stubs) — collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU util.
- 3/22: Deliver sizing deck + recommended reserved GPU commit options (2xH100 steady, 4xH100 peak autoscale) + cost delta for A100.
- 4/02: Legal & Procurement draft SLA redline.

Open questions / Blockers:
- Which GPU vendor for primary pool (Nimbus leaning to A100 for existing contracts) -> impacts reserve sizing and cost baseline.
- Procurement wants a 12-month committed price band; needs trade-offs for burst credits vs fixed reserve.
- Security needs engineered proof for data residency and retention purge APIs.

Quotes and shorthand from call:
- "We need predictable latency during earnings windows — sudden spikes are the risk." — Nimbus Head of Infra
- "If you can show 99.9% + clear burst play for events, procurement can move faster." — Procurement

Internal action items for Redwood team:
- SE (Liam): finalize perf harness + synthetic load generator configs; create balancer rules for canary fallback to smaller models.
- AE (Priya): schedule procurement cadence, collect SLA requirements doc.
- Security: send SOC2/ISO artifacts and schedule VPC test.

Attached stubs/refs:
- Drive: /drive/shared/pricing/nimbus-dedicated-workshop-2026.pdf
- Jira: DED-241 (tracking workshop infra), SEC-118 (security POC)
